Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

lean verb

rest one’s weight against or on something

also lean against, lean back, lean forward, lean over, leaning

classical

Liv. 4.19.4: hastā innīxus (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 2.27: scūtīs innīxī (Lewis & Short)

innītor, innītī, innīxus sum (innīsus sum)

verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative or the dative

lean or rest on, support oneself on

The prose word for resting one’s weight on a support: a stick, a spear, a column, someone’s arm (in Pansam frātrem innīxus, Plin. NH 7.182, Lewis & Short). Figuratively, to rely on. For pushing against something with the feet, see lean on.

Other words

  • acclīnis, acclīne — leaning against

    adjective, third declension, with the dative · also used · classical · Verg. A. 10.834: arboris acclīnis truncō (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā post Augustum)

  • inclīnō, inclīnāre, inclīnāvī, inclīnātum — bend, lean (the body, a thing) to one side

    verb, first conjugation, transitive; also intransitive, or with sē · also used · classical · Lucr. 2.243: paulum inclīnāre necesse est corpora (Lewis & Short); Liv. 36.44.2: mālōsque inclīnat (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: in the literal sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan; Cicero uses it figuratively, of opinion and fortune turning one way (sē ad Stōicōs inclīnāre, Fin. 3.10).

Examples

  • corpusque levābat arboris acclīnis truncō

    and he was easing his body, leaning against the trunk of a treeVerg. A. 10.833–834 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōlī mūrō innītī: tectōrium nōndum siccum est.

    Don’t lean on the wall: the plaster isn’t dry yet.composed

  • Baculō innīxus ambulat avus.

    Grandpa walks leaning on a stick.composed

See also lean on, bend.

SourcesLewis & Short: innitor · Lewis & Short: acclinis · Lewis & Short: inclino

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
